lead: Video-game hardware a person owns, organised by what the object does for play: consoles and handhelds, game media, controllers, accessories, modding and repair, VR & XR, and arcade and pinball machines; game titles live in the Interactive Entertainment taxonomy.

depts.t: Machines that play video games on a screen: TV consoles, handhelds, hybrids, built-in game units and the add-ons that extend them; a game disc or cartridge → Game media; a pad → Controllers; a gaming PC → Computers.
depts.ax: How is the machine played: on a TV from swappable games, in the hand, from games built into the unit, or as an add-on to another system?
depts.note: Organised platform → revision (model, slim, special edition) → region; titles are out of scope.

b.v: the system and its library (compatibility, backward compatibility) > performance for the price (resolution, frame rate; Pro against standard model) > disc or digital edition and storage > controller and screen
b.w: Carried over from the previous edition's buying order.

b.v: implementation (original hardware > FPGA > emulation) > video output > screen > build
b.w: Carried over; FPGA vs emulation is the standard collector distinction.

b.v: loose < boxed < complete in box (CIB) < sealed; region (NTSC-J, NTSC-U, PAL)
b.w: Usual collector-market grading, as in price guides such as PriceCharting.

s.t: Machines that connect to a TV and run swappable games, including set-top microconsoles and modern rebuilds of old systems; a handheld → Handhelds & hybrids.
s.ax: kinds by how the machine is built: original hardware, set-top microconsole, clone or FPGA rebuild

ax: What does the object do for video games: run the game, hold it, control it, protect or power the machine, alter it, put the player inside it, or stand in an arcade?
key: 1. Is it a machine that plays games on a TV, in the hand or from built-in games, or an add-on that changes what a console can read? → Consoles & handhelds
2. Is it the disc, cartridge or card that holds a game, or an edition, reprint, grade or copy of one? → Game media
3. Does the player drive the game through it with hands, feet or voice (pad, stick, wheel, gun, instrument)? → Controllers
4. Does it protect, power, hold or connect a console without changing what plays on it? → Accessories
5. Is it a part, kit or tool to load other media, sharpen the picture or repair a console? → Modding, repair & retro video
6. Is it worn on the head to show a virtual world, or an add-on for such a headset? → VR & XR
7. Is it a coin-operated cabinet, board, pinball machine or prize game? → Arcade & coin-op

Precedence: a flash cartridge is modding (step 5) before media (step 2); a VR controller stays with VR (step 6) before controllers (step 3); an arcade stick is a controller (step 3), while a bare arcade lever is an arcade part (step 7).
